deities: Lord Jagdish (Jagannath, a form of Vishnu)

history.summary: Built in 1651 by Maharana Jagat Singh I (ruled 1628-1653), the Jagdish Temple is the largest and most celebrated temple in Udaipur, standing on a tall terrace reached by 32 marble steps near the City Palace. Constructed in Indo-Aryan (Maru-Gurjara) style with a three-storied shikhara, it enshrines a four-armed black-stone idol of Lord Jagannath (Vishnu) with a brass Garuda image facing it and four subsidiary shrines (Ganesha, Surya, Shakti, Shiva). Contemporary inscriptions record a construction cost of Rs 1.5 million; parts of the shrine were damaged in Mughal attacks and later restored. Local belief holds the idol was excavated under a tree in Kunba village (Dungarpur). No duplicates of other CSV rows found.

town_description: Udaipur, the 'City of Lakes' in southern Rajasthan, was founded as the capital of the Mewar kingdom by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1559. Set among the Aravalli hills around Lake Pichola and Fateh Sagar, it is one of India's most visited heritage cities, known for its palaces, temples and old-city lanes.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport (Udaipur), about 22 km east.
travel.railway: Udaipur City railway station, about 2.5 km away.
travel.road: On City Palace Road in the old city, easily reached by taxi or auto-rickshaw from anywhere in Udaipur.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Most sources give 4:15 AM-1:00 PM and 5:15 PM-8:00 PM; one travel guide lists 5:00 AM-2:30 PM and 4:00 PM-10:30 PM (seasonal) - verify on arrival.
